options: Stages files for the next snapshot
Saves a snapshot with a message

m0-git.q: `git status` says 'nothing to commit, working tree clean'. What does it mean?
options: Error, you must force a commit
Everything is already saved, nothing pending
m0-git.why: Clean = working = staging = repo. You already committed.
why_wrong: Not an error, it's the ideal state.
Without a repo it would say 'not a git repository'.

m0-git.q: You get `error: remote origin already exists`. What happened?
options: An origin already exists, change the URL with remove/set-url instead of adding again
m0-git.why: `remote add` runs only once. To fix: `remove` + `add` or `set-url`.
why_wrong: The repo exists, only the local URL is duplicated.

m0-git.q: What must never be pushed to Git in this bootcamp?
m0-git.why: Real secrets never go to Git even if private. Only .example with CHANGEME.
why_wrong: Original composes are kept as docs.

options: Create lab/branch, commit, PR, merge into main
m0-git.why: main is what works. Experiment on a branch and merge via PR.
why_wrong: Without a commit there is nothing to push.

options: Receives 80/443 and routes to the right container + TLS
m1-docker.why: It's the doorman: reverse proxy + Let's Encrypt. Without it you'd expose 26 ports.
why_wrong: It doesn't run apps, it routes.

m1-docker.q: `docker volume ls` shows 2 volumes with 26 containers. Why?
options: They use bind mounts, invisible to volume ls, only seen in docker inspect Mounts
m1-docker.why: Binds like /home/...:/data don't show in volume ls. Check Mounts.

options: Localhost only, entered via Cloudflare Tunnel, not directly
m1-docker.why: 127.0.0.1 = host only. Cloudflared brings it in through an outbound tunnel.

m1-docker.q: Which command tells you where freshrss stores data on the host?
options: docker inspect freshrss with Mounts.Source and Destination
m1-docker.why: Mounts.Source=host, Destination=inside. ps only shows ports.

options: Updates images alone, dangerous without pinning versions
m1-docker.why: It watches the registry and recreates. Handy but can break postgres/n8n without notice.

options: Google Borg/Omega, released 2014 by Burns/Beda/McLuckie to CNCF
m2-k8s.why: Borg/Omega ran Google. K8s is its open version. Book Ch.1.

m2-k8s.q: You delete a Pod of a Deployment. What happens?
options: The controller creates another one alone
m2-k8s.why: Deployment keeps desired replicas. Pods are disposable (book Ch.2), PVC survives.
why_wrong: That's the magic vs docker run.

options: Service=stable internal IP, Ingress=HTTP entry by domain pointing to Services
m2-k8s.why: Pods change IP, Service doesn't. Ingress is the new nginx-proxy-manager.

options: ConfigMap=non-sensitive config in Git, Secret=passwords outside Git
m2-k8s.why: TZ/DATABASE_URL go in ConfigMap. ADMIN_PASSWORD/JWT only in the cluster. (Book doesn't cover these objects: our addition.)
Probes decide restart/traffic (book Ch.4). Deployment guarantees N alive.

options: 80/443 are already used by nginx-proxy-manager, they'd clash
m3-install.why: Two ingresses on the same ports = one won't start. We keep your edge.
why_wrong: Traefik is fine, it's a port conflict.

m3-install.why: Ready = kubelet ok. NotReady check journalctl -u k3s.
why_wrong: Pending is for Pods, not Nodes.

m3-install.q: Where does the k3s kubeconfig live?
m3-install.why: That file holds admin certs. Export KUBECONFIG to it. Never commit it.
Docker also uses containerd, but k3s doesn't need dockerd. Book Ch.1: K8s is the orchestrator, the runtime is the engine.

m3-install.q: If you mess up the install, how do you uninstall k3s without touching Docker?

options: Seeing logs of the already-dead container (CrashLoop)
m4-kubectl.why: Without --previous you only see the empty current one. The dead one holds the cause.

options: Wrong name/tag or private GHCR without imagePullSecrets
m4-kubectl.why: Describe will say 401 or not found. Check tag and docker-registry secret.

options: Tunnel only to your terminal to test without Ingress
m4-kubectl.why: Only your localhost. Ideal to validate before domains.

options: Seeing the history of what K8s tried and why it failed

m4-kubectl.q: `kubectl delete pod X` in a Deployment…
options: Recreates another pod alone, it's the self-healing test
m4-kubectl.why: The controller reconciles (book Ch.2: pods are disposable). That's why you never expose Pods directly.

options: Git on main is the truth, apply from file, no manual edits
m5-gitops.why: If they differ, Git wins with apply -f. Manual edits get lost. (Book Ch.9: git your manifests.)

m5-gitops.q: Why one namespace per app at the start?
options: delete ns wipes everything without touching other apps
m5-gitops.why: Isolates the blast radius when you break things. Book Ch.6 lesson: start simple before hardening.
Service finds Pods by labels. No match, empty.

m5-gitops.q: How do you store a Secret correctly?
options: kubectl create secret without committing, only .example in Git
m5-gitops.why: Real one only in the cluster. Only example with CHANGEME in repo. Book Ch.8 audits Secrets.

options: Idempotent, run it N times and it stays the same
m5-gitops.why: Declares desired state (book Ch.2: declarative model). Says created/configured/unchanged.

options: Official image, 1 volume, no build, low risk
m6-freshrss.why: No GHCR nor external DB. If you break it, re-import OPML.
1 node = RWO is enough. 2Gi is plenty, no RWX without NFS.
/ redirects and fails (book Ch.4: probes must hit a real endpoint). /i/ is the real home. /api/health belongs to saa-quiz.

options: Adjust runAsUser/fsGroup to 33 or 1000 per image
m6-freshrss.why: Volume owned by root and container runs without permission. fsGroup fixes it. Book Ch.8: audit security contexts.

options: Copy with deploy running at 1 replica
Scale to 0, copy to PV path, chown, scale to 1
m6-freshrss.why: Copying sqlite while running corrupts. Stopped is consistent. Book Ch.9: HA is not backup, migrate stopped.

options: build, only pull. That's why you push to GHCR
m7-saaquiz.why: build: . is compose-only. In K8s the image comes prebuilt via Actions.

m7-saaquiz.q: Empty JWT_SECRET_KEY in K8s with a new PVC causes…
options: Invalid tokens / logout because it generates another random one
m7-saaquiz.why: In Docker it survived thanks to the eternal volume. New PVC in K8s = new random. Pin it in a Secret.
Read-only root needs writable tmp. Privileged is the opposite of cap_drop. Book Ch.8: least privilege.
401 = no creds. Create a docker-registry secret in that namespace.
It's the compose healthcheck. FreshRSS uses /i/.

m8-actions.why: Parses without a cluster. Doesn't test business.

m8-actions.q: build-push only when code changes thanks to…
m8-actions.why: Avoids builds on docs changes. Book Ch.7: CI builds/pushes image, CD updates cluster.

m8-actions.q: To push to GHCR in Actions you use…
m8-actions.why: Ephemeral token with packages permission. No login gives denied.

m8-actions.q: CD with auto-apply from GitHub stays…
options: Off until 7 stable manual days, with runner + approval
m8-actions.why: Automating something broken breaks faster. Manual first. Book Ch.7: manual deploys don't scale, but only automate what works.

options: No, fix indentation/labels and wait for green
m8-actions.why: Branch protection requires green checks. Red = broken main.

m9-fin.q: How many apps do you shut down per day?
options: One only, 3-7 stable days before the next
m9-fin.why: Minimum blast radius. If K8s fails, only one rolls back to Docker.

m9-fin.q: Rolling back freshrss to Docker is…
options: delete ns + docker start + npm to the old upstream
m9-fin.why: The edge stays on npm. Switch upstream and start the old container. Book Ch.9: declarative resources revert, PVs may not.

m9-fin.q: What marks a module as passed in this app?
m9-fin.why: Without a real log there's no real migration.

options: SQLite can't handle 2 writers at once
m9-fin.why: 2 writers corrupt. Postgres scales. Book Ch.2: StatefulSets exist for sticky identity + storage.
